symptoms#0.title: Headache

cats.name: Simple analgesics (e.g., paracetamol, ibuprofen)
cats.why: May relieve mild tension-type headache if suitable for the person.

symptoms#0.refer: Sudden "worst ever" headache, stiff neck, confusion, weakness, head injury, visual disturbance, headache in pregnancy with swelling, or new headache over 50.

symptoms#0.title: Fever

cats.name: Antipyretic analgesics (paracetamol, ibuprofen)
cats.why: Can reduce fever and discomfort; choose age-appropriate formulations.

symptoms#0.refer: Infant under 3 months with ≥38 °C, fever > 3 days, non-blanching rash, breathing difficulty, stiff neck, drowsiness, or dehydration.

symptoms#0.title: Sore throat

cats.name: Simple analgesics
cats.why: May ease pain and fever if suitable.

symptoms#0.refer: Difficulty swallowing or breathing, drooling, high fever, symptoms > 1 week, or immunocompromised.

symptoms#0.title: Dry cough

cats.name: Cough suppressants (e.g., dextromethorphan)
cats.why: Considered for short-term dry cough in adults.

cats.name: Soothing linctus (glycerin/honey)
cats.why: Demulcent; can soothe an irritated throat.

symptoms#0.refer: Cough > 3 weeks, blood in phlegm, breathlessness, chest pain, weight loss, night sweats.

symptoms#0.title: Chesty cough
symptoms#0.refer: Green/bloody sputum with fever, breathlessness, chest pain, cough > 3 weeks.

symptoms#0.title: Cough
symptoms#0.refer: Cough > 3 weeks, blood, breathlessness, chest pain, weight loss, night sweats.

symptoms#0.title: Nasal congestion

cats.name: Steam inhalation (menthol/eucalyptus)
cats.why: May relieve the feeling of congestion.

symptoms#0.refer: Symptoms > 10 days, severe facial pain, high fever. Oral decongestants: avoid in high blood pressure.

symptoms#0.title: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever)

cats.name: Low-sedating antihistamines (cetirizine, loratadine, fexofenadine)
cats.why: Commonly used for hay fever; less drowsiness.

symptoms#0.refer: Wheeze, breathlessness, or no improvement with treatment.

symptoms#0.title: Heartburn / indigestion

cats.name: Antacids
cats.why: Neutralise stomach acid for quick relief.

cats.name: Alginates
cats.why: Form a protective raft over stomach contents.

symptoms#0.refer: Chest pain spreading to arm/jaw, difficulty swallowing, weight loss, vomiting blood, black stools, age > 55 with new symptoms.

symptoms#0.title: Diarrhoea

cats.name: Oral rehydration salts (ORS)
cats.why: Replaces fluids and electrolytes — first priority.

cats.name: Antimotility (loperamide) — adults only
cats.why: Short-term symptom relief if no blood or fever.

symptoms#0.refer: Blood in stool, high fever, signs of dehydration, infants/elderly, > 48 hours, recent travel with severe symptoms.

symptoms#0.title: Constipation

cats.name: Bulk-forming laxatives (ispaghula)
cats.why: Increase stool bulk; take with water.

symptoms#0.refer: Blood in stool, weight loss, severe pain, change in bowel habit > 2 weeks, age > 50 with new symptoms.

symptoms#0.title: Minor cuts & grazes

cats.name: Antiseptics
cats.why: Clean the wound to reduce infection risk.

symptoms#0.refer: Deep or gaping wounds, uncontrolled bleeding, animal bites, numbness, signs of infection.

symptoms#0.title: Minor burns

cats.name: Burn dressings / hydrogels
cats.why: Cover after cooling the burn for ~20 minutes under cool running water.

symptoms#0.refer: Large, deep, facial, hand, genital, electrical or chemical burns; burns in young children.

symptoms#0.title: Sprains & muscle pain

cats.name: Topical NSAIDs
cats.why: Local pain relief if no NSAID contraindications.

symptoms#0.refer: Cannot bear weight, deformity, severe swelling, numbness, back pain with leg weakness or bladder problems.

symptoms#0.title: Fungal skin infection
symptoms#0.refer: Nail involvement, widespread infection, diabetes, no improvement after 2 weeks.

symptoms#0.title: Itching & bites

cats.name: Mild hydrocortisone
cats.why: Short-term for inflammation (not on face/infected skin).

symptoms#0.refer: Swelling of lips/throat or breathing difficulty (emergency), spreading redness, fever.

symptoms#1.title: Sunburn
symptoms#1.refer: Extensive blistering, fever, chills, dizziness or confusion.

symptoms#1.title: Mouth ulcers

cats.name: Antiseptic mouthwash / local anaesthetic gel
cats.why: Ease pain and keep area clean.

symptoms#1.refer: Ulcer > 3 weeks, unexplained recurrent ulcers, painless or unusual ulcers.

cats.name: Head-lice lotions (dimeticone, permethrin)
cats.why: Applied as directed, repeated after 7 days.

symptoms#1.title: Nappy rash
symptoms#1.refer: Severe, blistered or spreading rash, or fever.

symptoms#1.title: Dry eyes
symptoms#1.refer: Pain, light sensitivity, reduced vision, contact-lens wearers with red eye.

symptoms#1.title: Ear wax
symptoms#1.refer: Ear pain, discharge, dizziness, possible perforation.

symptoms#1.title: Dry skin
symptoms#1.refer: Infected (weeping/crusted) skin, widespread eczema not controlled.

symptoms#1.title: Stopping smoking
symptoms#1.refer: Recent heart attack/stroke, pregnancy — seek advice.

symptoms#1.title: Toothache
symptoms#1.refer: Dentist for all toothache; urgently for facial swelling, fever or difficulty swallowing.

symptoms#1.title: Sleep problems

cats.name: Short-term sedating antihistamines (adults)
cats.why: Not for older adults; short term only.

symptoms#1.refer: Persistent insomnia, low mood, sleep apnoea symptoms.

symptoms#1.title: Chest pain
symptoms#1.refer: EMERGENCY: chest pain, especially spreading to arm/jaw with sweating, nausea or breathlessness — call emergency services.

symptoms#1.title: Breathlessness
symptoms#1.refer: Breathlessness, wheeze not relieved by inhaler, or inability to complete sentences — urgent medical/emergency care.

levels.title: Basic Pharmacy Navigation
levels.intro: Welcome to your first shift! Learn your way around the pharmacy. Use the joystick to walk, swipe to look around, and tap things to interact.

levels.title: Simple Customer Interactions
levels.intro: Customers are arriving. Listen, ask questions, and choose a suitable product.

levels.title: Medicine Information
levels.intro: Always read the medicine information before dispensing. Use the search to find products by name, ingredient or symptom.

levels.title: Multiple Customer Conditions
levels.intro: Customers now have more varied problems. Ask the right questions before deciding.

levels.title: Safety Checks
levels.intro: Some customers have allergies, conditions or medicines that make certain products unsafe. The safety check is your last line of defence.

levels.title: Inventory Management
levels.intro: Keep stock healthy: restock low items, remove expired stock and protect the cold chain.
objectives: Place a restock order at the POS
Handle the expired stock in storage

levels.title: Difficult Customer Scenarios
levels.intro: Not every problem can be solved over the counter. Recognise red flags and refer when needed.

levels.title: Advanced Pharmacy Simulation
levels.intro: A busy shift with prescriptions, stock problems and random events. Stay safe under pressure.

levels.title: Inspection Preparation
levels.intro: Inspections require 20/20. Study the training modules and pass a practice quiz before the official inspection.
objectives: Score 8/10 or more in a practice quiz

levels.title: 20-Question Inspection
levels.intro: The official pharmacy inspection. Every answer must be correct.
